question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this gateway-local multi-user identity, authorization, delegated-agent, and public plugin API model as the supported Teams v1 trust boundary?
rationale: The patch creates permanent gateway security, persistence, protocol, and plugin-SDK contracts; implementation tests cannot determine whether these responsibilities and trust assumptions match maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor after security review
options.body: Approve the direction only after a reviewed threat model, plugin API stability decision, upgrade and recovery plan, and real-gateway proof are attached.

options.title: Narrow to a private experiment
options.body: Keep Teams behind non-public internal seams and defer the durable public plugin contract until the trust model is validated.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Retain single-operator Workspaces and close or redesign this implementation if core multi-user identity is not currently sponsored.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after security review
recommendation.body: Approve the direction only after a reviewed threat model, plugin API stability decision, upgrade and recovery plan, and real-gateway proof are attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Workspaces foundation and its core, plugin, persistence, and UI ownership boundaries were established through this person's recent merged work.
